page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-192-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server configuration featuring 192 dedicated virtual CPUs and 720.0 GB of system memory. This allocation provides a resource density of 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates within the c4n server family and does not include any graphics processing units. Local storage is configured with NVMe SSDs, though a specific local storage capacity is not defined in the hardware profile.

With 192 dedicated vCPUs, this server type is designed for high-density parallel processing workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent computational resources without the performance degradation associated with shared-core environments. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high core count and balanced memory-to-core ratio offer a dense consolidation platform for large-scale deployments, reducing the overhead of managing multiple smaller instances.

This configuration is suitable for compute-heavy tasks that require substantial parallel processing capabilities and a moderate memory footprint. Applicable workloads include large-scale web serving, high-throughput batch processing, continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines, and distributed data processing tasks that do not require GPU acceleration.
